concepts.name: Reflection at Spherical Mirrors & Mirror Formula
concepts.summary: Image formation by concave and convex mirrors, Cartesian sign convention, and linear/longitudinal magnification.
concepts.common_traps: Concave mirror has negative focal length ($f < 0$); convex mirror has positive focal length ($f > 0$).
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Virtual image in a concave mirror is ALWAYS magnified ($|m| > 1$), while in a convex mirror it is ALWAYS diminished ($|m| < 1$).

concepts.name: Refraction at Interfaces, Snell's Law & TIR
concepts.summary: Snell's law, apparent depth shift in transparent media, and total internal reflection condition ($i \ge \theta_c$ from denser to rarer).
concepts.standard_formulas: n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r, \quad \sin\theta_c = \frac{n_2}{n_1} \; (n_1 > n_2), \quad d' = \frac{d}{\mu}, \quad \text{Shift} = t\left(1 - \frac{1}{\mu}\right)
concepts.common_traps: Total internal reflection can ONLY occur when light travels from an optically DENSER medium to a RARER medium.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Area of circle through which light emerges from fish/source at depth $h$: $A = \frac{\pi h^2}{\mu^2 - 1}$.

concepts.name: Lens Maker's Formula & Optical Instruments
concepts.summary: Thin lens refraction, Lens Maker's equation, lens power in Dioptres ($P = 1/f$), and magnifying power of optical devices.
concepts.common_traps: When a lens is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\mu_l > \mu_{\text{glass}}$, its converging/diverging nature REVERSES (convex acts concave).
concepts.tips_and_tricks: When a lens is cut vertically in half, each half retains the SAME focal length $f$. When cut horizontally, focal length remains $f$, but image brightness is halved.

concepts.name: Prism Dispersion & Minimum Deviation
concepts.summary: Ray refraction through triangular prisms, condition for minimum deviation ($i = e, r_1 = r_2 = A/2$), and angular dispersion.
concepts.common_traps: At minimum deviation, the refracted ray inside an equilateral prism passes strictly PARALLEL to the base.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Condition for no emergent ray (always TIR on second face): $A > 2\theta_c$.

### 2.1 Reflection at Spherical Mirrors & Mirror Formula (Mirrors)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **122 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Image formation by concave and convex mirrors, Cartesian sign convention, and linear/longitudinal magnification.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}, \quad m = -\frac{v}{u} = \frac{f}{f - u}, \quad f = \frac{R}{2}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Concave mirror has negative focal length ($f < 0$); convex mirror has positive focal length ($f > 0$).

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Virtual image in a concave mirror is ALWAYS magnified ($|m| > 1$), while in a convex mirror it is ALWAYS diminished ($|m| < 1$).

### 2.2 Refraction at Interfaces, Snell's Law & TIR (Refraction)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **110 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Snell's law, apparent depth shift in transparent media, and total internal reflection condition ($i \ge \theta_c$ from denser to rarer).

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r, \quad \sin\theta_c = \frac{n_2}{n_1} \; (n_1 > n_2), \quad d' = \frac{d}{\mu}, \quad \text{Shift} = t\left(1 - \frac{1}{\mu}\right)
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Total internal reflection can ONLY occur when light travels from an optically DENSER medium to a RARER medium.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Area of circle through which light emerges from fish/source at depth $h$: $A = \frac{\pi h^2}{\mu^2 - 1}$.

- **[2026 Morning Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"A spherical interface lens of radius $R$ separates two media of refractive indices 1 and 1.4 respectively as shown in the figure below. A po..."* — **Correct Answer: A**

- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"A convex lens is made from glass material having refractive index of 1.4 with same radius of curvature on both sides. The ratio of its focal..."* — **Correct Answer: D**

### 2.3 Lens Maker's Formula & Optical Instruments (Lenses & Instruments)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **70 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Thin lens refraction, Lens Maker's equation, lens power in Dioptres ($P = 1/f$), and magnifying power of optical devices.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\frac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right), \quad P = \frac{1}{f}, \quad M_{\text{telescope}} = \frac{f_o}{f_e}, \quad M_{\text{microscope}} = \frac{L}{f_o}\frac{D}{f_e}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: When a lens is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\mu_l > \mu_{\text{glass}}$, its converging/diverging nature REVERSES (convex acts concave).

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: When a lens is cut vertically in half, each half retains the SAME focal length $f$. When cut horizontally, focal length remains $f$, but image brightness is halved.

- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"A thin biconvex lens is prepared from the glass $(\mu=1.5)$ both curved surfaces of which have equal radii of 20 cm each. Left side surface ..."* — **Correct Answer: A**
- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"A thin convex lens and a thin concave lens are kept in contact and are co-axial. Which of the following statements is correct for this combi..."* — **Correct Answer: A**

### 2.4 Prism Dispersion & Minimum Deviation (Prisms)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **39 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Ray refraction through triangular prisms, condition for minimum deviation ($i = e, r_1 = r_2 = A/2$), and angular dispersion.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\delta = i + e - A, \quad \mu = \frac{\sin\left(\frac{A + \delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin(A/2)}, \quad \delta \approx (\mu - 1)A \; (\text{thin prism})
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: At minimum deviation, the refracted ray inside an equilateral prism passes strictly PARALLEL to the base.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Condition for no emergent ray (always TIR on second face): $A > 2\theta_c$.

- **[2026 Morning Shift] Q#4 (MCQ)**: *"A ray of light passing through an equilateral prism is having velocity $2.12 \times 10^{8}m/s$ in the prism material, then the minimum angle..."* — **Correct Answer: B**

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring JEE Mains Pitfalls in Geometrical Optics

### 1. Sign Convention & Vector Inversion Errors
Paper-setters frequently exploit sign confusion in energy and potential differences. Always write the fundamental thermodynamic / vector definition before substituting numerical values.

### 2. Unit System Discrepancies
Molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), SI vs CGS units, and micro/milli/nano multipliers (10^-3, 10^-6, 10^-9) account for over 35% of calculation mistakes in numerical type questions.

### 3. Boundary & Extreme Conditions
In transient circuits or limiting conditions (t=0+, t -> inf, infinite dilution, resonance), always check the asymptotic behavior of inductors, capacitors, and electrolyte mobility.

### 4. Direct Addition Fallacy
Never algebraically add intensive quantities (such as electrode potentials or AC component voltages) without accounting for electron weighting (n1*E1 + n2*E2 = n3*E3) or phasor vector geometry (V_total = sqrt(V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2)).
